title: State Epochs and Temporal Anchoring
summary: Work through State Epochs and Temporal Anchoring.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **State Epochs and Temporal Anchoring** in *Spatial Memory* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Spatial Memory, § State Epochs and Temporal Anchoring
blocks.md: A bounding box or 3D Gaussian pose emitted by a neural object detector describes where an entity was when photons struck the camera CMOS sensor, not where it is when the inference tensor arrives in memory. Every spatial claim refers to a specific physical instant, its **epoch**, and any state crossing a physical AI pipeline carries three distinct epochs before an actuator can fire.

questions.q: The section **State Epochs and Temporal Anchoring** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A ring buffer sized to the delay horizon lets the filter rewind to a late measurement's capture epoch, correct, and replay, and measurements older than the buffer are rejected.
A filter's reported covariance is a hypothesis tested offline by NEES against ground truth and online by NIS on innovations, and an above-band mean flags the safety-critical overconfident filter.
Every spatial claim carries evidence, estimate, and publication epochs, and only a physical measurement advances the evidence epoch, so prediction and republishing must preserve it.

When distinct state histories give identical measurements no estimator can separate them, and innovations stay near zero while the true state drifts, so observability must be designed in by excitation or added sensing.
